rationale: Baseline attempt-00 passed numerics, compiled, and simulated at 157.29 us with block_M=128, block_N=64, block_K=64, num_stages=1, threads=256, swizzle=0, smem=32768 bytes (at cap), 2 blocks/SM. M=128 means block_M=128 gives a single tile row, so panel swizzle reuse is moot there; retain block_M=16/32/64/128 to allow multi-row panels and parallelism. Keep block_N up to 256 (divides 4096) to test larger-N-launch trade-off, but drop 32 to focus. block_K includes 128 to probe the pipeline/register trade-off; num_stages raised to 2-4 (stage=1 gave limited pipeline overlap and 2 blocks/SM). threads reduced to 128/256 since 64 was unmeasured and 256 worked; feedback will disambiguate. swizzle expanded to [0,4,8,16] modestly since large panels may exceed cache and M/Q small; restrict from 32/64 for first post-baseline run. Weight traffic at 1.5 (DRAM 34.6 MB dominates) and launches at 0.5 (only ~0.5-1k blocks), keep pipeline and footprint at 1; shared_memory_limit left at 32768 (hard portability cap binds anyway, actual smem hit cap). Next hypothesis: longer pipeline with stage=4 and block_K=128 improves simulation latency; test thread-domain change (128 vs 256) and modest swizzle now that a row-major baseline exists. Note validation scope: Metal numerics executed the exact source/config, CUDA binary not executed, GB10 values are simulator estimates only.
